title: Notorious murder site 'will be bombarded with paranormal activity' this weekend
excerpt: Pendle Hill is one of the most haunted spots in Britain and paranormal experts say activity is already increasing in the lead up to Halloween night this coming weekend.

Pendle Hill is one of the most haunted spots in Britain and paranormal experts say activity is already increasing in the lead up to Halloween night this coming weekend.

Sian Hewitt

18:00, 29 Oct 2026

Ghost hunters say there is one area in the UK that is set to see a lot of action this Halloween - and it is where witches were once murdered. Pendle Hill is one of the most haunted spots in Britain and paranormal experts say activity is already increasing in the lead up to Halloween night this coming weekend.

‌

‌

The borough in Lancashire has been considered haunted ever since nine suspected witches were sent to their deaths there in 1612 - but in 2026 activity again is heating up in the area.

‌

Professional ghost hunter Robert Pulme said: "We have seen more reports of activity but this is always a very popular hotspot at Halloween.

‌

"But what many don't realise is that this area is busy all year round with visitors often making reports of feeling strange as they walk up to the top of the hill.

"Halloween increases the activity and I am sure judging by what we have seen in recent weeks, the witches could be back this Halloween night."

According to local legend in the area, those who visit Pendle Hill and climb the top of the 557m-high mini mountain often feel "uneasy", "terrified for no reason" and sometimes even lose their breath often out of nowhere. A total of 12 Lancastrians were accused of witchcraft in 1612, leading to one of England's deadliest witch trials.

"There are rumours of ghostly and phantom monks, while people have reportedly experienced breathing difficulties there," says Stephen Oldfield, a Lancashire historian and author who works as a tour guide there.

‌

"There's always been this atmosphere and spooky presence in Pendle Hill. It's like being in another country, even compared to West Lancashire."

‌

The area is an especially popular place to visit around Halloween, when ghost-hunters try to connect with spirits allegedly haunting the borough's village.

Mr Pulme added: "The spirits are strong in the area, there's no doubting it is a haunted place. It is one of the most haunted spots in the country. It is not for the faint hearted."

‌

The Pendle Hill trials remain some of the most famous and well-documented in English history, and the borough has never managed to shake its sinister past.

‌

For the 400th anniversary of the Pendle witch trials in 2012, local organisations funded the Pendle Witches' Way and the Lancashire Witches' Walk, which trace the imagined routes the accused may have taken to their imprisonment at Lancaster Castle.

During the trials, a nine-year-old girl named Jennet Device was one of the key witnesses to "weird goings on" in the village and gave testimony so convincing it doomed her mother, brother, sister and grandmother to death. Nine of the 12 accused were found guilty and hanged on Gallows Hill.

‌

"A lot has happened there," Pulme continued. "It is without doubt a place of extreme pain and fury - a deadly mix in terms of ghostly goings on."
